The core coupling is Micro/Nano Sensing x Local Repair x Structural Reliability. Every proposed integrated test is limited to unoccupied scaled habitat panels, damaged coupons, environmental chambers and supervised hardware-in-the-loop systems; no inhabited dwelling, nanorobotic building maintenance system or structural certification is claimed. The falsifiable candidate predicts higher independently verified fault recall without worsening preregistered post-repair air-quality recovery under equal inspection exposure, material supply, energy, sensing, computation, time and human-operations budgets. Repair success is separately conditional on load-path requalification, credible reference identity, moisture containment and a functioning physical stop. A controlled localized robotic repair system must compete with scheduled expert inspection, replace-on-failure maintenance and expert-performed local treatment. Concealed moisture, common-mode sensor drift, inaccessible crack ligaments, incompatible repair chemistry and hidden support fixtures are ways the hypothesis can fail. Negative specimens, refused states, destructive tests and incomplete repairs remain in the full denominator. Thirty mechanically and statistically distinct research plates include Paris-regime fatigue crack growth, mode-I and mixed-mode fracture, energy release, cohesive-interface work, load balance, fatigue survival, detection recall and false clearance, ultrasound and acoustic observability, thermal and moisture transport, contaminant mass balance, resin flow, cure kinetics, correlated uncertainty, materials and energy accounting, conditional causal effects and physically verified stop latency. Each mathematical plate states its mechanism, dimensional assumptions, independent reference, blinded contradiction and research-chapter links. The seed Paris relation da/dN = C(Delta K)^m is a conditional empirical model for particular fatigue regimes, not a universal law of repair or evidence that a crack has healed. Eighty-two chapters and 410 single-page investigations examine specimen provenance, hidden crack truth, fracture and fatigue, imaging and sensor drift, repair-material chemistry, robotic deposition, wall-module utility boundaries, environmental requalification, long-cycle maintenance and independent laboratory reconstruction. Two hundred individually worded Research Gates challenge different physical witnesses, resource-matched rivals, coupled faults, false-clear decisions and reproducibility limits. Thirty-three distinct Phoenix Answer Embryos propose separate future scientific objects, including fracture-reference capsules, moisture witnesses, cure validation rigs, aerosol exposure ledgers, physical interlocks and cross-site specimen relays. These are research proposals and evidence contracts, not demonstrated autonomous repair devices. The research is hypothetical, non-occupancy and intentionally vulnerable to refutation. Existing studies establish bounded robotic crack inspection and concrete sealing methods, polymer-glass simulation mechanisms, fatigue testing practices and material measurement approaches, but do not validate the integrated F41 architecture. items.summary: Unrefereed research candidate. A wide binary star takes thousands of years to complete one orbit, so its eccentricity usually cannot be found by following the orbit. Astronomers instead use the angle Γ between the pair's projected separation and projected relative velocity, whose distribution over many binaries depends on the population's eccentricity law. Hwang, Ting and Zakamska (MNRAS 2022, Appendix B) asked whether this angle distribution determines the eccentricity distribution uniquely. In the ideal model (random orbital phase, uniformly random 3D orientation, error-free projections) this package derives the likelihood of one angle in closed form, p(γ|e) = [acosh(1/e) − 1{|cos γ| > e} acosh(|cos γ|/e)] / (π sin²γ), and shows that its mixtures are classical Abel transforms. This gives an explicit inverse for every eccentricity law, including atoms: different eccentricity laws never give the same angle law. The inverse is continuous in the weak topology but discontinuous in total variation, so fine structure can be nearly invisible. Moments need no inversion: E√(1−e²) = (π/2) E sin³Γ and E e² = 1/2 + E cos 2Γ − (1/2) E cos 4Γ; these are the only symmetric unbiased single-angle observables for their targets and give near-efficient power-law index estimators. Two exact selection results bear on Gaia samples: thermal populations keep a uniform angle law under selections that ignore sky position angles, and binning by projected separation preserves the model under a log-uniform semimajor-axis law. The archive contains the 21-page manuscript (PDF and LaTeX source) with complete proofs, a Python library (likelihoods, observables, estimators, Kepler simulators), the full validation script with recorded results and figures, semantic negative controls, fast CI checks, the bounded novelty report and SHA-256 sums. All data are synthetic; no observational catalogue is analysed. Assurance boundary: written proofs; floating-point numerical checks and Kepler simulations; producer-side replay in normal and optimised modes; internal AI-assisted review (five roles, adversarial correctness review, proof audit and re-review). This is not peer review, independent reproduction or formal verification. Creator: Anonymous. Prose, manuscript and data CC0-1.0; code MIT.

Submission-ready reproducibility release for the PL-Seq reanalysis.

This version includes the revised manuscript source and title, complete Nature-style software references, the bioRxiv PDF build workflow, seven machine-readable supplementary tables, the renamed and updated Supplementary Figure 1 catalog, updated Figure 1 timeline, and stable Zenodo concept-DOI citation metadata.

All repository safety, syntax, and reviewed-figure checksum checks passed before release. This version adds the exact AMD64 Apptainer SIF used for FASTQ alignment, BAM processing, molecule filtering, and PSI reconstruction. The binary environment is accompanied by a SHA-256 checksum, embedded image labels, a command-derived software-version report, and usage documentation. The original Apptainer definition file was not retained; therefore, the archived SIF is the authoritative record of the executed computational environment. This version adds plseq-plotting.sif , a rebuildable Apptainer environment for programmatic PL-Seq and direct-RNA figure generation. It includes Python, Matplotlib, pyGenomeTracks, R plotting packages, Pandoc, and Poppler. The image passed embedded dependency tests, PNG/PDF artifact tests, and end-to-end rendering of the seven-page, 28-gene direct-RNA atlas.

items.summary: Pre-registered protocol (methods approved 2026-09-29; file sha256 e46e8cc4…) for a fresh-week confirmatory evaluation of frozen methods for inferring IPv6 sibling prefixes of IPv4 prefixes. Published before any evaluation-week data were read. Version 2 adds Amendment 1 (approved 2026-10-02): the published reference of validation week 20260616 is documented as an incomplete build; gates G1/V4 are decided on the three weeks with an intact reference. Published before gate G2 and before any evaluation-week data were read. Version 3 adds the freeze record (2026-10-02): gate G2 passed, reproduction check passed, code hashes frozen. Published before any evaluation-week data were read. Version 4 (2026-10-03) adds the results and the code. It was published after the evaluation: the analysis code; per-query outputs and statistics of all evaluations (E1, E2, E3); the plan, addenda and outputs of the post hoc analyses that followed E3; the completed freeze record (Steps 5–8); and a complete list of deviations and exposures with a map between the names used in the article and those of the code (DEVIATIONS_AND_NAMES.md). The exposures to evaluation-week information that preceded the protocol (aggregate counts of one archive day, file listings) are stated in the protocol, section E3.0, and in DEVIATIONS_AND_NAMES.md. Version 5 (2026-10-03) adds three post hoc items that were run after version 4 under a sixth addendum (posthoc_e3_addendum6_20261003.md): a correction of the ceiling definition, an analysis of Tor pairs that never occur as RIPE Atlas pairs, and the hypotheses without the week of 2026-07-07; their scripts and outputs; the configuration files; an updated list of deviations (items 27 to 29); and a runbook (RUNBOOK.md) with scripts that regenerate the numbers, tables and figures of the article from the released outputs. The result archives of version 4 are unchanged. The published list of validation week 2026-06-16 is called "an incomplete build" in the paragraph on version 2 above and in Amendment 1; that was the name used at the time. What was observed is lower coverage than the list rebuilt from the sources; the cause is not confirmed by OpenINTEL (see the note in DEVIATIONS_AND_NAMES.md, section 6). Version 6 (2026-10-31) adds the reproducibility extension for Sections S8–S11 of the supplement of the article “TRACE6: Tiered Ranking and Persistence-Controlled Evaluation of Probe-Reported IPv4–IPv6 Prefix Associations” (s8-s11-reproducibility-extension-v6.tar.gz), and the plans and amendments of the S8 and S9 analyses as written (protocol_history_s8_s11.tar.gz). All were specified after the E3 results were known and are descriptive. The archive holds plans, code, provenance records, saved outputs and replay commands that recompute every reported S9–S11 interval and mean and regenerate the S8 tables; it does not refit models or rebuild raw inputs. Withheld: the private-storage module of the E4 run controller (see WITHHELD_FILES.md in the archive); no reported number depends on it. README.md and SHA256SUMS are updated; all other files of version 5 are unchanged.

items.summary: The magnetotelluric (MT) method uses natural electromagnetic field variations to image subsurface electrical resistivity at depths ranging from tens of metres to hundreds of kilometres. It is widely used in geophysical exploration for natural resources, including minerals, geothermal energy, and groundwater, as well as in the characterisation of sites for CO$_2$ storage and in studies of crustal and lithospheric structure. The MT inverse problem is, however, inherently non-unique: many distinct resistivity models reproduce the observations equally well. Conventional practice nonetheless reports a single regularised model, with no quantitative measure of its uncertainty. MTGeophysics.jl is a Julia package developed to address this limitation. Its principal aim is the quantification of uncertainty in MT model building, advancing interpretation from a single deterministic model, through an ensemble of plausible models, towards the full posterior distribution. The package also provides tools for data analysis, mesh generation, masking, forward modelling, inversion, model analysis and visualisation for MT research and applications. items.summary: This dataset provides the numerical results and supporting data for the simulation studies presented in the manuscript "Identifiability and Scheduling for Shared-Timestamp Polynomial Sensor Calibration". The dataset includes: 1. Paired-sensor calibration results, including trial-level measurements, summary statistics, and bootstrap confidence intervals. 2. Parameter sensitivity analysis results, including trial-level data and aggregated performance summaries under different experimental conditions. 3. Identifiability analysis results for symmetric timestamp configurations, including numerical rank evaluation. 4. Supporting figures generated from the computational experiments. All numerical datasets are provided in CSV format to facilitate inspection, independent analysis, and reproducibility. The accompanying figures provide visual representations of the experimental results. These data support the evaluation of sensor calibration performance, parameter sensitivity, statistical reliability, and identifiability under shared-timestamp scheduling configurations. The associated computational scripts and execution environment are documented in the companion Code Ocean capsule, which has been submitted for reproducibility verification.

items.summary: Artificial intelligence (AI) agents embedded in software-as-a-service (SaaS) platforms inherit the user's permissions. When a permission is revoked during a task, the platform rejects the next read, but the agent still retains the data it previously retrieved in its context, drafts, saved documents, and memory. This study examined how platforms can enforce a mid-task revocation on that working state. The author defined correct behavior for four revocation types, each mapped to an obligation to block, purge, or suspend, including leaks through paraphrases, aggregates, and existence hints. The author built RevBench, a simulated field-service platform, and compared nine enforcement designs from access control, information-flow control, and machine unlearning on six frontier models in 6,048 runs. Outputs were scored using exact matching and two large-language-model judges. Per-call authorization still failed in 417 of 720 runs (57.9%), rising from 34.4% when the revocation preceded retrieval to 72.8% when it followed delivery. Information-flow labels leaked the least (12.9%) but left revoked data saved in 44.2% of runs. Designs that invalidated the context performed best, while editing the context in place left derived facts behind. A full restart and selective replay with listing-level provenance reached 21.4% and 21.0% substantive failure, the latter with 12.1% fewer model calls. Most remaining failures were disclosures about the restriction, often repeating the platform’s own notice, and larger models did not reduce them. SaaS platforms need revocation controls that reach the agent’s working state and match the type of revocation. items.summary: Abstract: Classical inferential statistics and p-value hypothesis testing in healthcare big data repositories suffer from severe structural limitations, notably p-hacking, asymptotic N-bias, and the frequent violation of independent and identically distributed (i.i.d.) assumptions due to intra-patient longitudinal dependencies, hospital clustering, and epidemiological shockwaves. To overcome these failures, we introduce an Inverse Breakpoint Analysis, a scale-invariant, physics-inspired metrological audit framework. Our analysis treats discrete clinical event counts not as abstract probabilities, but as physical informational mass. Grounded in Garwood exact discrete limits and Wilson-Hilferty approximations, the framework extends our previous work on stress testing indices for Big health data and establishes three rigorous thresholds: a pure mass saturation limit, a baseline tolerance band, and a structural signal threshold. Through the use of these three parameters, our inverse break-point analysis eliminates false-positive artifacts induced by massive repository sizes while preventing under-powering in small cohorts. Ultimately, the framework demonstrates that percentage-based thresholds are kinematic artifacts of scale, whereas absolute excess discrete mass serves as the sole physical invariant for healthcare data validation. We validated this approach with numerous illustrative examples.
items.title: Inverse Breakpoint Analysis: A Scale-Invariant Physics-Inspired Metrological Audit for Sanitary Big Data

items.summary: Next Generation Risk Assessment (NGRA) requires the integration of increasingly heterogeneous evidence from New Approach Methodologies (NAMs), computational models, chemical information, biological mechanisms and exposure assessment. RISK-HUNT3R WP9 has addressed a fundamental challenge for this transition: how to organise, connect and reuse diverse scientific information so that it can support transparent, reproducible and human-relevant safety assessment. The RISK-HUNT3R Knowledge Infrastructure provides a FAIR-oriented digital environment for managing and connecting experimental data, methods, compounds, computational resources and mechanistic knowledge. Its architecture combines harmonised data and metadata templates, controlled vocabularies and ontologies, compound and methods databases, BioStudies and EdelweissData integration, knowledge graphs, computational tools, AI assistance resources and cloud-based services. Together these resources support the progression from data capture and curation to analysis, mechanistic interpretation and evidence integration. The infrastructure has been deployed across distributed project partners to support collaborative research and reuse of RISK-HUNT3R and legacy EU-ToxRisk resources. A central principle emerging from this work is that effective NGRA infrastructure must support more than FAIR data. Methods, models, workflows, provenance, applicability and uncertainty also need to be captured so that scientific results can be interpreted within their Context of Use and assembled into evidence supporting a decision. Resources including ToxTemp, compound and methods databases, knowledge graphs, EdelweissData and ASPA-based workflows provide complementary components of this evolving evidence architecture. The resulting infrastructure provides both an operational resource for RISK-HUNT3R and a foundation for future development. By connecting data, methods, models and mechanistic knowledge through interoperable digital resources, RISK-HUNT3R demonstrates a pathway from fragmented NAM outputs towards reusable evidence workflows supporting transparent NGRA.
items.title: From NAM Data to Trusted Evidence: RISK-HUNT3R Knowledge Infrastructure for Next Generation Risk Assessment

items.summary: This repository provides three physics-based datasets for developing and evaluating surrogate models to identify the seismic failure modes (SFMs) of coastal reinforced concrete bridge bents supported by pile-group foundations under combined scour and corrosion. Each sample contains 20 input variables: 17 structural and geotechnical parameters, scour depth, and the corrosion levels of longitudinal and transverse column reinforcement. The output is one of three SFMs: column flexural failure (CFF), foundation flexural failure (FFF), or column shear-associated failure (CSF). These labels are determined through nonlinear finite element analysis and code-based shear capacity calculations. The datasets support reproducible surrogate model development and subsequent life-cycle probabilistic assessment of SFMs and their transitions in deteriorating coastal bridge bents.

items.summary: A phase-only spatial light modulator in the pupil of a microscope objective can form hundreds to thousands of optical traps at once, but only if the phase pattern it displays is computed well: the pattern fixes how much light reaches the traps, how equal the traps are, where stray light goes, how the pattern survives a real device, and how fast it can be recomputed when traps move. DinHot is an open studio that runs 24 methods (19 published ones and 5 proposed here) on the same task, with the same seeds, metrics and device model, in Python as the reference and in a TypeScript port that runs live in a browser. We describe the optical and device model, the methods with the measured acceptance of each, 14 cases from a 3 x 3 array to a disordered 819-trap array and shaped potentials, the benchmark protocol, two learned models, and the 5 proposed methods, three of which meet their acceptance criteria on their acceptance tasks, each within a scope that the benchmark or the scope measurements narrow (a device-aware weighted Gerchberg-Saxton update, a flicker-bounded phase-continuous sequence and an efficiency-uniformity front), one of which meets a narrowed criterion (an aberration-robust hologram) and one of which is refuted by measurement (a learned warm start for phase-fixed weighted GS). A network trained on three-plane volumes beats its baseline at equal wall-clock on all 162 held-out volumes (median accuracy ratio 1.140), whereas its two-dimensional counterpart ties with Gerchberg-Saxton (ratio 0.9994). The model is a scalar Fourier model of a simulated device, not a calibrated instrument. Interactive studio and reproducible pipeline (Apache-2.0): https://github.com/fsantibanezleal/CEFOP_DinHot . Interactive studio: https://dinhot.fasl-work.com .

items.summary: Artificial intelligence (AI) agents embedded in software-as-a-service (SaaS) platforms inherit the user's permissions. When a permission is revoked during a task, the platform rejects the next read, but the agent still retains the data it previously retrieved in its context, drafts, saved documents, and memory. This study examined how platforms can enforce a mid-task revocation on that working state. The author defined correct behavior for four revocation types, each mapped to an obligation to block, purge, or suspend, including leaks through paraphrases, aggregates, and existence hints. The author built RevBench, a simulated field-service platform, and compared nine enforcement designs from access control, information-flow control, and machine unlearning on six frontier models in 6,048 runs. Outputs were scored using exact matching and two large-language-model judges. Per-call authorization still failed in 417 of 720 runs (57.9%), rising from 34.4% when the revocation preceded retrieval to 72.8% when it followed delivery. Information-flow labels leaked the least (12.9%) but left revoked data saved in 44.2% of runs. Designs that invalidated the context performed best, while editing the context in place left derived facts behind. A full restart and selective replay with listing-level provenance reached 21.4% and 21.0% substantive failure, the latter with 12.1% fewer model calls. Most remaining failures were disclosures about the restriction, often repeating the platform’s own notice, and larger models did not reduce them. SaaS platforms need revocation controls that reach the agent’s working state and match the type of revocation. items.summary: Phase-fixed weighted Gerchberg-Saxton (WGS) is the practical method for large arrays of optical traps, but it optimizes the hologram on an ideal model of the spatial light modulator (SLM), and the sequences that move traps interpolate between holograms that were never optimized for the frames in between. We test two hypotheses against the strongest baselines on the same scalar Fourier model. First, keeping the WGS weights but replacing the phase update by conjugate-gradient steps through the pixel-crosstalk kernel and the phase quantizer of the device (device-aware WGS) lowers the trap-intensity spread on the device. On a 10 x 10 lattice behind a crosstalk device, the relative standard deviation falls from a median of 5.21 percent for phase-fixed WGS at 30 iterations (5.21 percent at 100) to 0.205 percent, a median factor of 26 over 5 seeds (range 16 to 33) at a median 0.995 of the baseline's efficiency; the factor is 7.9 with 4-bit phase and a fill factor of 0.85 added, and 2.0 on a smaller 8 x 8 grid with flicker added and a fixed 30-iteration budget (the ratio of the means of 3 seeds); over the 5 geometries of the studio's benchmark on that device the median factor is 1.73 (0.97 to 4.69), and 2 of them meet both thresholds. A control that removes the device model from the loop gains nothing (5.14 percent), so the gain comes from the model. Second, optimizing every intermediate hologram of a moving-trap sequence with the trap phases locked to a smooth trajectory (flicker-bounded sequence) keeps the minimum transient intensity of the moving traps at a median 0.920 of their mean (range 0.915 to 0.932) over 5 seeds at 13 frames (below 0.9 at seven frames), against 0.654 (0.551 to 0.709) for linear phase interpolation. On longer moves, with the frames that keep the peak step per frame at most 0.2 Fourier units, the bound is met on 6 and 6 of 8 seeds of two lattice moves and on 5 of 6 seeds of a rearrangement case; the seeds that miss it miss it on the phase path their end phases prescribe, and at an equal number of frames on the rearrangement linear phase interpolation leads. Both results hold in a model of a simulated device and in a transient model that we define; neither is a hardware measurement. items.summary: Code and results for the paper "Leakage-Aware, Edge-Deployable Brain Tumor MRI Classification: A Latency, Accuracy and Calibration Benchmark". Motivation: Ashwini et al. (doi:10.1155/acis/2622873) note that most current brain tumor segmentation and classification methods rely on offline, static imaging and therefore do not support real-time monitoring. That paper reports results on the Kaggle Brain Tumor MRI dataset (7,023 scans: pituitary, glioma, meningioma and no tumor). This record addresses part of that gap by measuring per-image CPU latency of four classifiers, as a proxy for real-time capability, and by checking whether duplicate images inflate reported accuracy. Contents: a pipeline that audits the dataset for exact and near-duplicate images, builds naive and leakage-aware splits, fine-tunes MobileNetV3, EfficientNet-B0, ResNet50 and Inception-ResNet-v2 over three seeds, measures batch-1 CPU latency, and evaluates calibration. Folders: results (main 24 runs; 7,215 images, duplicate distance 0) and results_laptop (reduced MobileNetV3 runs; 7,200 images, duplicate distance 1). The MRI images are not included; the dataset is on Kaggle (doi:10.34740/KAGGLE/DSV/2645886). See README.md for the run order.

items.summary: The calibration and test probabilities of every run of a tabular classification benchmark, released so that prediction sets and their metrics can be recomputed without refitting a model. A conformal set is a function of four arrays: the class probabilities and labels on a calibration split, and the same on a test split. This deposit is those arrays, together with the software that reads them. The benchmark comprises 218 classification datasets and 22 models from four families, among them 13 tabular foundation models, each evaluated with the same ten seeds. Of the 218, 178 are real datasets and 40 are a synthetic block generated for this benchmark; three of the real ones are Bayesian-network resamplings of small classical datasets and are much larger than their seeds; of those, only one has its own seed in the collection, so that pair is not independent of itself while a rank test treats datasets as independent. Dataset size does not indicate provenance: the largest datasets in the collection are real. Coverage is not uniform and the per-model dataset count is reported for every cell. Eleven datasets carry more than ten classes, and the in-context models measured on them cannot enter them: one refuses and names the limit, another builds a ten-output head and fails inside a kernel. That is a capability limit observed on the models that were run rather than a property claimed of the family, and it is not missing work. One foundation model is measured on the original datasets only. Anything computed across models should be computed on a complete submatrix: the datasets on which every model being compared has all ten seeds. The calibration rows are held out of fitting, of tuning, of early stopping and of the in-context data, and each cell records which rows they were. The code that does it is included, with the line of each step documented. Probabilities are float64 and are not rounded: a prediction set is a comparison against a threshold, and a point sitting on that threshold moves if the value it is compared to is shortened. The data are released under CC BY 4.0. The software included in the source archive is released under the MIT licence, as stated by the LICENSE file it contains. The datasets themselves are not redistributed: each cell carries the row indices into its source dataset, and the synthetic datasets regenerate from their seeds with an included script. Model weights are not redistributed; every checkpoint is named in the model table. Version 1.2.0 adds the runs completed after version 1.1.0 and changes or removes nothing in it. Three new shards (cells-011 to cells-013, 2.02 GB) hold 311 further cells; index.parquet now lists all 46,182 cells and manifest_1016.parquet is their manifest. The files prefixed blocks_1016__ recompute the two blocks outside the main comparison on the completed runs, with the pipeline that produced the article's tables: the large-dataset block on 49 datasets and 21 models (42 in version 1.1.0) and the many-class block on 11 datasets and 7 models (5 in version 1.1.0). The main block of 113 real datasets and 22 models is unchanged. CHANGELOG.md lists what is added and the pairs that are still missing, with the reason for each.

items.summary: 50/60 MISSION RELIABILITY IN AUTONOMOUS NANOROBOTIC REGENERATIVE MANUFACTURING AT THE LIMIT MISSION RELIABILITY IN AUTONOMOUS NANOROBOTIC REGENERATIVE MANUFACTURING AT THE LIMIT is a 777-page English-language Research Design Working Edition in the STARLI Micro/Nanorobot Fabrication and Regenerative Biomanufacturing Sixty-Flagship series (Flagship 50/60). It investigates safe failure recovery with preserved productive service. The research coupling is autonomous manufacturing mission x regenerative specimen integrity x physically verified fault recovery. All proposed work is restricted to nonclinical in-vitro, organ-on-chip, synthetic phantom or authorized ex-vivo environments. No experiments were executed in preparing this edition; no human treatment, clinical efficacy or regulatory clearance is claimed. Its falsifiable candidate is: A frozen safety and recovery protocol will improve completed qualified work at equal fault burden while meeting independent stop and specimen integrity gates. The Atlas minimum demonstrator is: Blind-inject four fault classes into complete cell assembly missions with matched useful work targets. Strong comparators include expert human operation, fixed automation scripts and conventional redundant hardware. A central rival account is apparent safety caused by aborting early and completing less useful work. The nonnegotiable stop condition is: no advantage at equal effective work or an unknown fault fails to stop the apparatus. Each failed, aborted, hidden-fault and incomplete run is retained in the experimental denominator, and observation of a finished form is never substituted for independently measured function. Thirty mathematical plates address domain-specific metrics and established model families across transport, measurement, elasticity, time-dependent dynamics, causal attribution, calibration and uncertainty. Eighty-two chapters and 410 separately paginated scientific investigations organize six research arcs. Two hundred Research Gates have been revised with independent observables, one of fifteen blinded causal intervention families, orthogonal controls and noncompensatory refusal criteria. Thirty mathematical plates now carry model-specific physical derivation commentary, explicit applicability limits and distinct flagship-level blind checks. Thirty-three Phoenix Answer Embryos propose unbuilt future instruments and succession artifacts, each requiring its own bench validation. This version is a research design and not a report of validated physical findings. It draws scientific method and conceptual boundaries from the user-supplied Atlas and research mother volumes; especially the Atlas-supplied ancestry DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23046134 and 10.5281/zenodo.23486020. Full external bibliographic DOI checking and scientific peer review have not been completed. Domain-specific sensitivity, causal identifiability and independent replication require qualified laboratory evaluation before any scientific superiority claim. items.summary: Online sensor telemetry feeds the digital-twin, forecasting, control, and maintenance tools of instrumented water infrastructure. Probes deployed in these assets silently accumulate drift, flatlines, volatility bursts, and outages that existing pipelines often miss, because detectors and imputers are evaluated separately and under inflated synthetic metrics, and decay is treated as isolated events. This work proposes HARDIO, a Health-Aware Reliable Detection-Imputation Orchestrator, an operational data-quality framework that pairs a duration-weighted sensor decay scorecard with a per-variable, chained detector-imputer benchmark. The assignment is selected by a four-pillar composite score (operational 35%, health coverage 30%, reconstruction 20%, calibration 15%) that scores the signal an operator actually receives after detection and imputation. HARDIO processes sensor installations independently, enabling parallel execution and avoiding the need to evaluate all plant channels jointly. HARDIO is validated on the Cheles wastewater treatment plant (WWTP), a real 1,177 population-equivalent (PE) plant, over 432 days, 19 channels, and eight sensor installations. No single detector-imputer pair is best for every channel, so detection and chained imputation distribute across SAITS, KNN Residual, and LSTM-AE. Chained quality is reported for all 19 channels using 1-NRMSE; relative R² is interpreted on the 16 channels where the signal variance makes it meaningful, and 12 of these exceed R²=0.90. On the held-out final 20% of the record (12 channels in five installations), HARDIO achieves a mean chained 1-NRMSE of 0.976, within 0.0035 of a per-channel oracle, and outperforms the uniform SAITS pipeline (p=0.003). Its reconstruction performance is close to that of the strongest uniform pipelines, without a statistically significant improvement over them, and slightly below that of a single detector-imputer pair selected on validation data (0.978). The released artefact exposes the model map, confidence labels, margins, and production masks for decision support.

items.summary: LONG-TERM HABITABILITY OF MORPHING AUTONOMOUS MOBILE HABITATS AT THE LIMIT Chinese Title / 中文書名:可變形移動居住系統長期宜居性極限 56/90 LONG-TERM HABITABILITY OF MORPHING AUTONOMOUS MOBILE HABITATS AT THE LIMIT is a 777-page English Research Working Edition in the STARLI YULI Nano Supercar Trilogy (Research Institute XXXVI, Flagship 56 of 90). It investigates whether a traceable unoccupied morphing habitat testbed can improve the joint coverage of measured thermal, airflow, moisture, energy and structural engineering envelopes across controlled seasonal sequences while preserving independently reconstructable module identity. Its core coupling is Human-Comfort Proxy Models x Environmental Control x Longitudinal Test Evidence. The project uses guarded coupons, scaled modules, environmental chambers, inert-water and tracer-air circuits, and hardware-in-the-loop tests; it does not observe residents or establish an occupancy certificate. The preregisterable hypothesis is that, under matched materials, energy reserves, maintenance, sensor access, control computation and test time, a frozen morphing environmental-control policy will improve complete-cohort comfort-envelope proxy coverage without worsening module-identity continuity relative to competent static-habitat and expert manual-reconfiguration baselines. The supplied selective-risk candidate R_sel(tau)=E[L(yhat,y)|c>=tau] must be published with accepted coverage, so a low risk score cannot be purchased by refusing nearly every difficult climate or aging case. Hidden trials vary aging gaskets, radiant asymmetry, tracer-air pockets, power outages, sensor common-mode drift, broken connectors, incorrect material identity and ineffective physical stop contacts. Thirty mechanism-specific mathematical plates analyze heat balance, conductive and radiant transfer, operative temperature proxies, vapor mass and dew-point margins, air exchange, ventilation pressure, energy and water closure, sound, light, fatigue, reliability, stale information, uncertainty covariance, selective-risk coverage, tail excursions and second-site reconstruction. Eighty-two chapters contain 410 separately paginated investigations spanning material aging, climate control, indoor-environment proxy limitations, repair, operator authority and versioned evidence. Two hundred Research Gates formulate disconfirmable experimental questions across concealed faults, equal-resource comparisons and two-mechanism interfaces. Thirty-three distinct Phoenix Answer Embryos propose separately falsifiable future rigs, calibration artifacts, safe-stop witnesses and successor evidence packages. The volume is a prospective research design rather than a completed experimental study. An unoccupied thermal or tracer-gas rig cannot establish human comfort, healthy air, habitable water, fire and structural compliance, actual multiyear life, or a right to place people inside a mobile dwelling. The 777-page layout and enumerated items are structurally checked, but a language-duplication audit finds reused long editorial method spans; semantic uniqueness, physical modeling and all evidence inferences remain subject to deeper independent review. Relevant independently identified method references include Fanger (1973), DOI 10.1136/oem.30.4.313; de Dear and Brager (2001), DOI 10.1007/s004840100093; Brager and de Dear (1998), DOI 10.1016/S0378-7788(97)00053-4; Dang, Janssen and Roels (2024), DOI 10.1007/s12273-024-1176-8; Dang et al. (2025), DOI 10.1016/j.buildenv.2025.112867; and Broughton and Maxwell (2023), DOI 10.47120/npl.mgpg103. Standards ISO 7730:2025, ASHRAE 55-2023, and ASHRAE 62.1/62.2-2025 provide bounded normative context, not F56 verification. items.summary: Next Generation Risk Assessment (NGRA) requires the integration of increasingly heterogeneous evidence from New Approach Methodologies (NAMs), computational models, chemical information, biological mechanisms and exposure assessment. RISK-HUNT3R WP9 has addressed a fundamental challenge for this transition: how to organise, connect and reuse diverse scientific information so that it can support transparent, reproducible and human-relevant safety assessment. The RISK-HUNT3R Knowledge Infrastructure provides a FAIR-oriented digital environment for managing and connecting experimental data, methods, compounds, computational resources and mechanistic knowledge. Its architecture combines harmonised data and metadata templates, controlled vocabularies and ontologies, compound and methods databases, BioStudies and EdelweissData integration, knowledge graphs, computational tools, AI assistance resources and cloud-based services. Together these resources support the progression from data capture and curation to analysis, mechanistic interpretation and evidence integration. The infrastructure has been deployed across distributed project partners to support collaborative research and reuse of RISK-HUNT3R and legacy EU-ToxRisk resources. A central principle emerging from this work is that effective NGRA infrastructure must support more than FAIR data. Methods, models, workflows, provenance, applicability and uncertainty also need to be captured so that scientific results can be interpreted within their Context of Use and assembled into evidence supporting a decision. Resources including ToxTemp, compound and methods databases, knowledge graphs, EdelweissData and ASPA-based workflows provide complementary components of this evolving evidence architecture. The resulting infrastructure provides both an operational resource for RISK-HUNT3R and a foundation for future development. By connecting data, methods, models and mechanistic knowledge through interoperable digital resources, RISK-HUNT3R demonstrates a pathway from fragmented NAM outputs towards reusable evidence workflows supporting transparent NGRA.
items.title: From NAM Data to Trusted Evidence: RISK-HUNT3R Knowledge Infrastructure for Next Generation Risk Assessment
